title: finding(sdui-parser): the generated JSX types do not compile over the real public manifest — `RecordAlertProps` redeclares `visible` wider than `SduiBaseProps` (TS2430)
body:
Filing-gate category: ① a product defect with a named site, class (a). `reach:` named real producer: `generateDts`, a published export of `@object-ui/sdui-parser` documented as "the JSX type surface for authoring", run over the real public manifest (`manifestFromConfigs` over the console's public registration graph, 107 types). Reader: triage first (grade and route), then the seat that dispatches it. Filed by `domain:ui` seat 2 (`session_011p7ikEivgXefNDaE5S5Uec`) from the objectui#11044 dev report (PR objectui#11072, `out_of_scope_findings`), confirmed by that PR's contract review as pre-existing and not the PR's. ⛔ Not graded here.

## The site

Read at objectui `origin/main` `51c294958`:
- `packages/sdui-parser/src/codegen.ts` emits `SduiBaseProps` with `visible?: boolean`. `visible` is an every-node base member, so it gets no `Omit` in a declaring interface's `extends` clause. objectui#11044 added that `Omit` only for the six where-undeclared members.
- `packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx`, the `record:alert` registration, declares `visible` with `type: ['boolean', 'string', 'object']`. objectui#9100 measured those three arms against the installed spec's `ComponentPropsMap['record:alert']`, and the renderer honours all three through `toPredicateInput`.
- `generateDts` therefore emits `interface RecordAlertProps extends SduiBaseProps` with `visible?: boolean | string | object`.

## Measured (the objectui#11044 dev)

- `tsc --strict` without `skipLibCheck` over the `sdui-intrinsics.d.ts` that `generateDts` produces from the real public manifest fails with `TS2430 Interface 'RecordAlertProps' incorrectly extends interface 'SduiBaseProps'`: the types of property `visible` are incompatible.
- The result is identical at the PR's base and at its head.
- `packages/sdui-parser/scripts/gen-manifest.ts` `buildArtifacts` writes exactly this file.

Consumers: none found in objectui outside tests. `buildArtifacts` has no caller, and objectstack has no `generateDts` consumer. The published function and its documented output are the reach.

## Why it matters

The generated `.d.ts` is the authoring type surface, and it does not type-check as generated. An author (or an AI) who compiles against it gets an error inside the generated file rather than a check on their own JSX. With `skipLibCheck` on, the base interface's `boolean` hides the declared string and envelope arms.

## Direction (for triage, not a ruling)

The objectui#11044 rule, "a declared input wins with its type", is not yet applied to every-node members. Two routes:
- Extend that PR's `Omit` form to every-node members an interface declares.
- Widen `SduiBaseProps.visible`, and its predicate siblings `disabled` and `hidden`, to the predicate union `BaseSchema` admits.

The objectui#11044 contract review noted that `visible`, `disabled` and `hidden` are typed `boolean` on the JSX surface although `BaseSchema` also admits a predicate, and that widening them is a separate decision. Pin: the generated `.d.ts` over the real public manifest compiles under `tsc --strict` with zero diagnostics. objectui#11072 already has an in-memory `tsc` pin over a synthetic manifest to extend.

## Dedupe

The 1100 most recently updated objectui issues and PRs, open and closed (down to #2231), were listed via REST and grepped locally:
- `TS2430`: 1 hit, PR objectui#11072 (the source report);
- `incorrectly extends`: the same 1;
- `RecordAlertProps`: 3 hits, PR objectui#11072, PR objectui#11031 (the flat `body` refusal) and PR objectui#10502 (the CTA lookup); neither of the older two touches `visible` or the generated types;
- `SduiBaseProps`: 3 hits, objectui#11044, PR objectui#11072 and PR objectui#11042;
- `generateDts`: 3 hits, objectui#11044, PR objectui#11072 and PR objectui#10753;
- `skipLibCheck`: 1 hit, PR objectui#11072;
- lit control `record:alert`: 18 hits; absent control `zzqq_never_written_token_4242`: 0.

None carries the TS2430.
